brief: Tonight is Legs A, and it is the first Legs A since 20 August — 22 days, and a different gym. That matters more than anything else on the card: four of tonight's lifts happen only on Legs A, so the numbers your app would have shown you were all read off machines in the building you left on 2 September. Left alone it would have asked you for 300 on the calf press, where six days ago on the sled you will actually be standing at you did 260. So most of tonight's numbers have moved, and none of it is a step backwards in strength — it is the same effort written in the new gym's numbers. Leg press starts at 140 to let you feel the machine, then 180, then 200 as the working set; that is lower than your old 240 because the one new-gym leg press reading you have came in about 20 lb under the old machine for the same movement, and because yesterday's deadlifts came in a rep down on every set. Leg extension is a blank slate — nobody has touched that machine here — so take 105, then 135, and log what the pin actually says; that becomes next week's real number instead of an inherited one. Calf press is 260 across, not 300. The hip abductor goes up to 142.5, because you finished 135 for fifteen here on 5 September and that earns the next pin. Leg curl, hip adductor, cable crunch and the Bulgarians are unchanged — those machines and dumbbells read the same at both gyms. Two cues. On the Bulgarians, weaker leg first and match it, never beat it. On the calf press, pause at the bottom instead of bouncing. One ask: put your bodyweight in. The last reading is 23 August at 207, nineteen days ago, and with the show on 1 March that is the one number your trainers keep having to guess at.

flags.note: First Legs A in 22 days, and the first one at the new gym. Six of tonight's nine lifts are machines, and every machine number the app had was read at the old gym.
Left alone your calf press card would have said 300. On 5 September, on this gym's sled, you did 240, 260 and 260. Tonight asks 260.
Nobody has read the leg extension machine at this gym, not once. Tonight's 105 and 135 are a deliberate baseline, not a prescription — log the pin you actually use.

Yesterday's deadlifts came in under 28 August on every set: 235 for five not six, 255 for four not five, and three sets instead of four. That is 24 hours before a leg night, and it is why the leg press tops out at 200.

Your recovery trainer argued for two sets of Bulgarian split squats tonight instead of three. I kept three, because three is the count you accepted on 15 August and a prefilled card is not the place to quietly undo your own answer.

The ask to rename the Legs B opener to Deadlift is withdrawn. It was put to you on 6, 7, 8 and 10 September; your 10 September session landed afterwards and showed the deadlift shedding a set and a rep per set, so a second barbell pull off the floor each cycle is the wrong thing to add now.

Two cards will keep saying "Smith" for lifts you now do with a barbell — the Push A incline press and the Pull B row. There is no barbell press or barbell row in the app's exercise list, so no trainer here can write you an honest swap. Changing that needs the list itself edited.
Bodyweight last logged 23 August at 207, nineteen days ago and flat since 21 July. The show is 1 March.
Meso 2, week 3 of 4, a build block. Deload starts 21 September. All three trainers reported; five disagreements, all settled, and no pain or injury objection.

proposals.why: Your two leg days are the same day from the fourth lift on, so Legs A gives up the hanging leg raise and keeps the cable crunch while Legs B keeps both, which finally makes the two days different and takes tonight from 24 sets down to 22.

On 2 September you pressed dumbbells in this slot and wrote "New gym. No smith machine. Dumbbell press", so the Push B opener takes the name of the lift you are actually doing and asks for 4 sets of 8 to 10 instead of the smith bar's 6 to 8 — the name and the rep ask change, nothing else.

This is two sets stuck at the same 10 pounds since August with the reps sliding down, and Push B already gives you three sets of dumbbell lateral raises, which is the lift you told us on 23 August you thought was getting too many sets for such a small muscle.

overrides.reason: The 180/220/240 here was read at the old gym on 20 August. The one leg press reading you have at this gym came in about 20 lb under the old machine for the same movement, you have not done this lift in 22 days, and yesterday's deadlifts were a rep down on every set. 140 is the feel-it set, 200 is the work. If 200 for ten is easy, say so and it moves next week.
Dumbbells weigh the same at both gyms, so 17.5 carries over honestly. Last time you got 9, 9 and 8 against an ask of ten, so the weight stays and the job is the reps. Weaker leg first, then match it.

This is the one lift the app already had right at this gym: 145 is a weight that does not even exist on the old machine's stack. Open at 130 and hold 145. The fourth set is the new one, so ten is the target there, not twelve.

Nobody has read this machine at this gym, so tonight is the reading. 105 to find it, then 135. Take fifteen with about two left in the tank and log the pin you actually used — that sets the real number next week instead of the old gym's 150.
Same reading at both gyms: 105 for twelve on 20 August and 105 for twelve again here on 5 September. Weight stays, the job is one more rep. Two sets of fifteen earns 112.5.
You finished 135 for fifteen on this machine on 5 September, which is the top of the range, so you have earned the next pin.

Do not load 300 — that is the old sled. On this one, six days ago, you did 240 for fifteen, 260 for fifteen, then 260 for thirteen. 260 across tonight; three clean fifteens earns 280 next Legs A. Pause at the bottom, no bounce.
Cables did not change scale in the move and 65 is already your number here. You did 65 for ten three times on 5 September, the floor of the range, so stay at 65 and add a rep to the first two sets.

dissent.progression: Ramp to 220 — the new sled reads about 11 percent under the old one, so 220 is the honest translation of the 240 he pressed on 20 August.
dissent.recovery: Stop at 200, and vetoed the figure 240 outright on fatigue grounds.
dissent.why: Recovery brought a fact that did not exist when progression set its rule: the 10 September deadlift landed in the repo after yesterday's packet was written, and it shows every set a rep down and a fourth set missing. That is the posterior chain 24 hours out, stacked on 22 days off this lift and a sled he has never used feet-low. One pin light on a calibration night costs a week; one pin heavy on an unfamiliar machine after three weeks off costs the block. The veto was fatigue, not pain, so I could have overruled it — I did not, because the evidence behind it is new and specific.

dissent.progression: Three sets at 17.5, chasing the ten reps he has never hit on this lift.
dissent.recovery: Two sets tonight only — 22 days off, a new bench and rack, and he has never finished three at the asked reps.
dissent.why: Both seats want the same weight, so this was only ever about the set count — and the set count is not mine to cut. He was asked on 15 August whether this should be three sets and he accepted three. An override that quietly prints two would undo his own answer with no card to argue back at, which is the exact failure this repo has been burned by before. Recovery's case is real and it is in the notice bar where he can see it; if it should become two sets, that is a card he answers, not a number I slide past him.

dissent.progression: Ramp 105 then 135 — treat tonight as the reading, the way he opened the leg press and leg curl at this gym.
dissent.recovery: Flat 130 twice, hedged as “130 or the nearest notch under it if 130 is not there”.
dissent.why: Both seats agree nobody has read this machine, so the question is only which shape of guess teaches us the most. A ramp is how he actually calibrates — 120/140/160 on the leg press and 100/130/145 on the leg curl, both on 5 September — and it gives two data points instead of one. It also survives either stack: 105 and 135 are real pins whether this machine steps in fives or sevens-and-a-half, while 130 only exists if it steps in fives, which is why recovery had to hedge its own number.

dissent.progression: Up to 142.5 — he closed 135 for fifteen at this gym, the top of the range, which earns the pin.
dissent.recovery: Hold 135, no objection to the card as printed.
dissent.why: Recovery held without offering a number or any fatigue evidence aimed at this lift; it called the existing card fine rather than arguing against a rise. Progression has the stronger case and it is a plain one: fifteen reps at the top of the range on this exact machine six days ago is the definition of earning the next step. Nothing about a 22-day layoff touches a two-set hip machine.

dissent.progression: 260 then 280 twice — he hit fifteen at 260, so the next pin is earned.
dissent.why: Progression is right that 260 for fifteen earns a step, but it read only the sets that succeeded. The third set at 260 on 5 September came in at thirteen, under the fifteen the card asks. Putting 280 on sets two and three asks for more than he has shown on a fatigued set, on a sled he has stood at exactly once. 260 across is the honest ask, and three clean fifteens earns 280 next week on evidence instead of on a projection.
